approvedAuthority.sliceTitle: Provider-neutral application lock and Windows Hello

outcome: The native supervisor remains the sole application-unlock authority behind a provider-neutral verification contract. The existing non-persisting Windows-password path retains current-process SID equality, while the Windows Hello adapter uses the OS-owned desktop HWND consent API, reports truthful typed availability and adverse outcomes, and has no application access to PIN or biometric material. Only a current-generation native success may restart Core and unlock; cancellation, denial, unavailability, busy, failure, panic, stale generation, or Core-start failure remains locked without fallback.

integrationChecks.result: All 35 native library tests passed. The union covers password-provider parity and SID authority, every Windows Hello availability and verification result, absence of prompting when unavailable or windowless, success-only Core start/unlock, one-attempt reservation and backoff, stale-generation replay denial, Core-stop recovery, provider panic cleanup, startup/manual/inactivity/restart behavior, audit redaction, and native protection of supervisor/support boundaries.

All 15 focused renderer/runtime tests passed. Strict snapshot and Hello-availability decoding rejects accessors, coercion, unknown values, and malformed envelopes, while native-success-only reconciliation and fail-closed lock state remain intact.

All 15 selected security, profile-contract, and Windows credential tests passed, with one expected redirected-vault symlink case skipped because directory symlinks are unavailable to the current Windows token. The checks cover the HWND-bound Hello/no-secret/no-fallback source boundary, native protected-action authority, exact v1 profile, same-SID password recovery, secret zeroing, fail-closed corruption, and redacted bounded audit.

The real Windows x64 OS boundary returned exactly {schemaVersion:'1.0', provider:'windows-hello', availability:'not-present'}. This host cannot establish configured interactive Hello success, so no success is inferred or fabricated.

integrationChecks.command: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --lib --locked --offline -- -D warnings; desktop TypeScript --noEmit; desktop lint; architecture_check.py --repo .
integrationChecks.result: Rust formatting and warnings-denied Clippy, strict desktop TypeScript, desktop lint, and architecture validation passed. Architecture reports 13 areas, 12 modules, five stable interfaces, and three deployment profiles.

adversarialBoundary.successAuthority: Only VerificationOutcome::Succeeded from the reserved current native generation may start Core; the generation is checked again after Core start before unlock publication.
adversarialBoundary.failureAuthority: Cancellation, denial, unavailable, busy, failed, provider panic, lock race, Core-start failure, and unknown Windows results retain or restore locked state and cannot invoke another provider.
adversarialBoundary.secretBoundary: The Hello adapter receives only an application-owned HWND and a fixed content-free prompt. It receives no PIN, biometric, username, password, token, renderer-supplied provider, or renderer-supplied outcome.
adversarialBoundary.recoveryBoundary: Windows-password recovery is a distinct argument-free command that reuses the unchanged non-persisting current-process EqualSid verifier. It is not invoked by Hello or the primary Hello path and remains subject to deliberate selection in W1.A05.T04.
adversarialBoundary.crossProcessBoundary: Native availability and unlock snapshots are versioned and strictly reconstructed by the renderer; accessors, symbols, extra/missing fields, coercible objects, and unknown future success-like values are rejected fail-closed.

profileSelection.selected: This slice closes an authentication/security boundary and a native/renderer contract. The selected union therefore covers native lifecycle and provider mapping, strict cross-process decoding, same-SID recovery, real Windows availability, credential non-capture, concurrency/replay/Core-stop paths, compilation/lint/type checks, and architecture.
profileSelection.deferredToWaveExit: The complete cross-capability W1 happy, failure, denial, cancellation, migration, restart, recovery, security, accessibility, performance, packaging, and Windows x64 matrix remains mandatory at Wave exit. A configured interactive Windows Hello success prompt is conditional on release-authoritative hardware where the real availability probe reports available.

residualLimitations: Configured interactive Windows Hello success is unavailable on this host because the real OS probe reports not-present; injected native success and all adverse mappings are deterministic and pass, while real configured success remains a conditional W1 platform obligation.
Persisted provider selection and safe policy transitions are W1.A05.T03; the approved settings, deliberate recovery, focus, and accessibility experience is W1.A05.T04.
The complete cross-capability W1 qualification matrix remains due at Wave exit.
The unrelated untracked historical W1.A04.B00 witness remains protected and untouched.

downstreamHandoff.contract: provider-neutral native verification, typed Windows Hello availability/outcomes, current-generation success authority, unchanged same-SID Windows-password recovery, and fail-closed adverse behavior
strict versioned renderer/native availability and unlock contracts with no renderer-supplied authority, no silent fallback, and separate deliberate password recovery
